sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Nechtan, also named Elcmar, was an Irish god or hero. He figures in the tale of the goddess Boand. The river Boyne rises near a small hillfort called Sid Nechtain, a fairy mound shared with him. Some writers equate him with the more celebrated god Nuada. He once dwelt with his wife Boand in the great stone tomb named Bru na Boinne. Boand wished to lie with the powerful god Dagda, so she tricked Nechtan. The pair eloped, and the Dagda held the sun still for nine months, letting their child arrive before Nechtan learned of the affair. That child was Aonghus Og, who later duped Nechtan into surrendering Bru na Boinne on the plea that he alone had received no fairy dwelling.

okr.objective: Nechtan is an Irish god whose legend turns on the loss of Bru na Boinne.
